# [Baseline] - MAC - D - Apple Intelligence Restricted

Turns off Apple Intelligence features that have text, email, notes, web pages or images processed by a language model or sent to an external AI service, and keeps dictation on the device.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | macOS |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Settings Catalog |
| Assignment | — |
| Source | CIS Apple macOS 26.0 Tahoe Benchmark v1.1.0 L1 2.5.1.1–2.5.1.4 and 2.18.1 (mSCP branch tahoe); ids and values identical to OpenIntuneBaseline macOS v2.0 beta — SC - Device Security - D - Restrictions, except Safari summaries (OIB: on, here off) |
| File | [`Baseline_MAC_D_Apple_Intelligence_Restricted.json`](Baseline_MAC_D_Apple_Intelligence_Restricted.json) |

> **Alternative to [Baseline] - MAC - D - Apple Intelligence Permitted** — that one sets the same twelve settings to the opposite value. Assigning both results in a Conflict, and then neither does anything. Checked: [Baseline] - MAC - D - Restrictions (OpenIntuneBaseline macOS v1.0) sets none of these twelve ids, and no other template does. Siri is already off there (allowAssistant), so the ChatGPT integration via Siri was already largely closed; this policy also closes the integration in Writing Tools and signing in to an external service. Profile keys (com.apple.applicationaccess) and not DDM: in September 2026 Apple marks all twelve keys as deprecated from 26.4 onwards, in favour of the declarative configurations com.apple.configuration.intelligence.settings and com.apple.configuration.external-intelligence.settings (in Intune: intelligencesettings_* and externalintelligencesettings_*, which also exist for macOS). The profile keys nevertheless stay, and that has been worked through rather than postponed: those DDM configurations only exist from macOS 26.4 and Apple only allows them with supervised enrollment, whereas this payload also works on macOS 15 and on a Mac the user enrolled themselves. Converting now would leave Apple Intelligence unrestricted on 15.x and on 26.0 to 26.3, which is a regression. Deprecated does not mean removed at Apple either: the keys still work, and mSCP and OpenIntuneBaseline v2.0 beta use the same ones. Switch over once the fleet is on 26.4 or later and enrolled via ADE; then convert the whole policy and do not mix the two forms. The conversion is one-to-one: intelligencesettings_allowwritingtools, _allowgenmoji, _allowimageplayground, _allowappleintelligencereport and _forceondeviceonlydictation, the summaries under intelligencesettings_apps_mail, _apps_notes and _apps_safari, and externalintelligencesettings_enabled and _allowsignin. DDM can in addition do things this payload cannot (AllowImageWand, AllowVisualIntelligence, AllowPersonalizedHandwritingResults, ForceOnDeviceOnlyTranslation, Apps/Calendar), and that is a new choice, not part of the conversion. [Baseline] - IOS - D - Apple Intelligence Restricted is already declarative; there was no coverage of older versions to lose there. According to Apple, allowMailSummary only blocks manually summarising an email, not the automatic summaries. Anyone who does want to allow the ChatGPT integration, but only with the organisation's own business workspace, uses allowedExternalIntelligenceWorkspaceIDs — organisation-specific, so not included. Apple Intelligence only runs on Macs with Apple silicon and macOS 15.1 or later; on other Macs the settings do nothing. All are also valid on iOS/iPadOS; this policy is for macOS only. Deliberate deviation from OpenIntuneBaseline v2.0 beta: it leaves allowSafariSummary at true; false here, because a summarised web page may be an intranet or SharePoint page. The Apple Intelligence report (allowAppleIntelligenceReport) is off, as in OIB.
